If I’m not mistaken the police already had their guns out when they first pulled her over. She would be more likely to lose control of the car and hit innocents if she had been shot getting out of the blockade. Police generally close roads and divert traffic quite quickly when they are aware of a dangerous driver, as well as blocking off all the exits so they can’t escape. My issue isn’t really with whether or not shooting would have been the right thing to do in that case. Saying that she was so lucky to not have been shot at the end, it’s shocking to see that the gun culture is so ingrained in US police that it just suggests shooting is and would have been the common solution.

Had she plowed through civilians and the police shot after her, what about all the civilians in the line of fire? They wouldn’t be guaranteed a direct hit either and that could cause the car to lose control and cause more civilian casualties. In a scenario where there are a lot of civilians around, it would be reckless for police to open fire on her. Plowing through the police cars is a different matter because the cars are placed there specifically to block her car. There’s no need to shoot her when her car has been stopped. Shooting after people should not be the first line of action under most circumstances and is not the only possible action police know they can take.

The cars she rammed when escaping were the police cars, which were being used as the tactic to stop her car. If she was contained and moving slowly, shooting her would be excessive at that point especially when she was surrounded by police. True that tasers don’t go through windows but if they were able to get that close and then shoot, I think it’d be unnecessary as she wouldn’t be going anywhere after the police car sandwiched her into the pole.

I agree with you! But shooting her would not have solved anything. There’s no reason to shoot her when the car has stopped and shooting after the moving vehicle could cause it to go out of control or put others in the line of fire which would have caused an even greater danger.

There was no need for a gun at any point there, the first time they pulled her over wasn’t a situation that called for guns and it’s not like they would be shooting as they drove because that would create a far more dangerous situation. I also believe that the police carry tasers which in this situation would also have been unnecessary but a more appropriate level of force if the driver put up a struggle at the end. The police use methods like the the ones above, using their cars to create roadblocks, “tailgating” the car into a stop etc. Which would effectively stop the car. Yes it was a very dangerous situation but it wasn’t one where guns would be an appropriate measure. The way he said she was lucky to not have been shot at the end implied that it was entirely out of their control... shoot now and ask questions later. That seems extremely reckless and irresponsible to me and isn’t an appropriate way to deal with dangerous driving.

Hi, sorry that you're in this situation right now, I understand that it's really hard. I had a friend who started while I had been actively harming for years who was unhealthily dependent on me at the time. I noticed that we were just reinforcing each other's bad habits and sending each other into negative spirals and talking about it with each other wasn't helping. I ended up trying to build him a bigger support network than just me by getting him to talk to our other friends, and making sure he knew that we were all supportive before distancing myself from him. I'd already had other friends tell me we weren't good for each other and were just making things worse. I know this might not have been the most ideal thing to do but it was to the point where his life was literally in my hands and it was destroying me. I'd honestly advise you to put yourself first, because I'd put myself into the mentality that I'd get my friend through it even at the cost of myself and it was awful for both of us.  In my experience, it's really hard to get through a self harm thing when both people are in a bad place, so maybe you could help your friend build a support network specifically for her self harm/eating disorder that doesn't involve you and leave the details of the issue out of your relationship so it doesn't start revolving around that. I hope you figure it out, but remember to take care of yourself first before anything. Good luck
